Jenny Picking Cockles

This transcription has been given the wrong key sig. It shouldn’t have B flats. This is why I complain about people cutting & pasting direct from Henrik Norbeck’s tune index (where the correct version is, by the way). You’re simply lifting the transcription with complete disregard for - and lack of understanding of - it’s content. Shame cuz it’s such a great tune.

A very different setting

The setting by b.maloney seems to be so different as to be a another tune altogether than the other ones. That version is the tune I was expecting to find under Jenny’s Picking Cockles and it’s certainly the setting played by le Ceoltóiri Cultúrlainne (item 16 under the ‘recordings’ link). I wonder which versions the other recordings use?

↳ Posted by Angebangsthedrum on March 21st, 2013.

I just listened to the 17 recordings of Jenny Picking Cockles in my iTunes library. All except one is basically the tune posted by Brad Maloney. That includes Danny O‘Mahony, Willie Clancy, Leon Agnew/Pat O’Connor/Dave Flynn, Willie Kelly/Mike Rafferty/Donal Clancy, Cohmaltas Ceoltóirí Éireann, Troy MacGillivray, Jimmy Power, Tommy McCarthy, Joe Derrane/Carl Hession, Ronan Browne/Peter O‘Loughlin, Terry Bingham, Patrick Street, Tulla Ceili Band, Conor McCarthy/Christie Barry/Cyril O’Donoghue, Mike Rafferty, Chris Sherburn/Denny Bartley, Graham Dunne, and Frankie Gavin.

Only Roisin McGrory/Damian Harrigan from one of the Fiddle Music of Donegal discs is the other very different setting from Dr. Dow and others.

↳ Posted by GaryAMartin on March 21st, 2013.

Jenny Cocklepickers

I’ve recordings of these fellows having at this reel:

David Power
Jimmy Power
Joe Cooley
Joe Derrane

Martin O’Connor
Mick and Denis O’Brien
Mike Rafferty
Neil O’Boyle
Peter Carberry
Peter Laban
Robbie Hannon
Ronan Browne and Peadar O’Loughlin
Sean McKiernan
Sean Reid and Peadar O’Loughlin
Sean Talty
Sean Talty and Eamonn McGivney
Terry Bingham
Tomas and Seosamh O’Ceannabhain
Willie Clancy
Willie Kelly & Mike Rafferty with Donal Clancy

B Maloney’s version is the one in D is the one in O’Neill’s in all probability don’t care to bother to check is the one Willie Clancy liked to play is the one most often recorded here. Neillidh Boyle called the tune he played after the Pigeon on the Gate Jenny Picking Cockles which is transcribed above in a variety of ways which is occasionally heard still which should have its own entry as the relation between these tunes is a bit tenuous.

Re: Jenny Picking Cockles

See Ceol Rince na hÉireann II.277 for a Sliabh Luachra version collected from Mrs Murphy in Ballydesmond. She called it the Old Slipper Shoe ((An tSeanbhróigín Bhog) Denis Murphy’s name for it was Johnnie Seán the Rake. It’s maybe sufficiently different to merit a separate entry if currently being played in a session.

Re: Jenny Picking Cockles

These recordings are of the other JPC:

Foinn Seisiún 4 by Ceoltóirí Cultúrlainne
Late… In The Night by Christy Barry, Conor McCarthy, Cyril O’Donoghue
Ceol Ar an bhFeadóg Stáin by Donncha O’Briain
Donncha O’Briain by Donncha O’Briain
Return To Inis Mor by Joe Derrane
Traditional Irish Music From London by John Blake, Lamond Gillespie And Mick Leahy
The Fort Of Kincora by Martin Connolly and Maureen Glynn
At Home With Mickey Doherty by Mickey Doherty
In Full Spate by Paddy Glackin
The Primrose Glen by Preston Howard Wilde
Number 6 by Sean Potts
Ó Aird go hAird by Tomás Ó Ceannabháin, Seosamh Ó Ceannabháin
Sporting Nell by Tommy McCarthy
The Fiddle Music Of Donegal - Volume Two by Various Artists
It Was Mighty : CD #1 by Various Artists
Irish Dance Music - Folkways LP by Various Artists
The Pipering Of Willie Clancy. Vol 1 by Willie Clancy
The Gold Ring - CD 1 Of 2 by Willie Clancy
The New Broom by Willie Kelly And Mike Rafferty With Donal Clancy

Many of the others belong there too, I bet. This tune derives from Donegal’s Nelidh Boyle and very few have played it since - I was surprised that Mickey Doherty and Paddy Glackin don’t. Verena Commins & Julie Langan do, I have their record. Also Roisin McGrory & Damian Harrigan on the The Fiddle Music of Donegal, Volume Two. I don’t have the Altan but it’s on YT of course: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lFquskpaQYU
